summary: Only 34959823 meets the eligibility rule: a randomized double-blind crossover in young healthy adults in which a single 1.5 g Nitrosigine dose improved total RBANS and immediate memory (the primary aim) but no other domains, with internal reporting discrepancies (16 vs 19 completers; 8 vs 12 g dextrose). It supports a narrow acute focus/memory credit. The FMD study (32093766) is a vascular surrogate and the TMT studies (27869715) report mostly within-group changes without a designated primary outcome; both are approved without credit.

applicability.studied_population: Young healthy adults (about 18-28) taking a single 1.5 g dose of Nitrosigine before cognitive testing.

identity.standardization: Inositol-stabilized arginine silicate (ASI); not isolated arginine

population.description: Young healthy adults (University of Arkansas), mean age about 21 (range 18-28), 63% female; abstract reports 19 completed, Methods report 19 enrolled and 16 completed both trials.

study_contexts.study_design: Randomized double-blind placebo-controlled crossover; single dose, cognitive tests before and 60 minutes after; trials at least 7 days apart.

outcomes.name: Primary aim cognitive battery: total RBANS and immediate memory improved vs placebo (repeated-measures ANOVA, p<0.05)
Other RBANS domains and digital cognitive assessments: no significant differences

limitations: Single acute 1.5 g dose in young healthy adults; no evidence for chronic use, older adults or sustained energy.
Reporting discrepancies retained: completers 19 (abstract) vs 16 of 19 (Methods); dextrose vehicle 12 g (abstract) vs 8 g (Methods), present in both arms.
Small, company-linked evidence base; exact Nitrosigine only.
Returned decision A014: source-content hold; methods now verified from full text.
Dr. Pham's fourth ruling set (2026-10-28): limited, outcome-specific acute cognition credit for the exact Nitrosigine formula only.
Context authored and source-verified by agent review (Claude) on 2026-10-28; Dr. Pham's pre-approval of fully source-verified contexts attested by Sean on 2026-10-28.

outcomes.name: Flow-mediated dilation (the study's purpose): supplement x time p<0.001; Nitrosigine +31% vs placebo -2%; allometric scaled +23% vs 0.60%

limitations: Acute endothelial surrogate in young active adults; not cardiovascular-health, blood-pressure or exercise-performance evidence; no designated primary outcome label.
